title: Is CES 2026 worth attending? Questions, alternatives and discounts you need to be aware of
summary: What happens in Vegas shows up in your store. Learn what CES is and what CES 2027 means for online sellers’ January prices.
body_markdown:
They say what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas. Every January, the tech industry flies in to prove that saying is wrong.


The occasion is CES, the show once known as the Consumer Electronics Show. But ask two people about CES 2026, and you might get two very different reviews. The[first person could be having](https://www.reddit.com/r/CESLV/comments/1qaloqe/ces_2026_is_in_the_books_and_i_had_an_amazing_time/) the week of their life:


*“CES 2026 was the best one ever! Made plenty of new connections, had many companies provide me samples of their products to help promote their brand, and went to some amazing parties including the Snapchat one with Snoop Dogg, Amazon one with Florida and Ke$ha, and Yahoo with Public Enemy!”*


But t[he second person might be having different thoughts](https://www.reddit.com/r/CESLV/comments/1q6wmkn/ces_2026_lacking_and_slacking/)


entirely:


*"Yes we get it; AI this and AI that. Everything Ai. Cool. Is there anything else here? All of the robots are identical and everyone has an autonomous vehicle. Most of the live demos were failures. Some booths even made you download apps to waste your time. What happened to the testing tracks? This was an extremely lackluster event."*


Honestly, both of them have a point.


CES is where tech brands go to show off what they plan to sell this year, and sometimes things they’ll never sell at all. CES 2026 drew 148,392 participants by the organizer’s[independently audited count](https://www.ces.tech/press-releases/ces-2026-audit-shows-four-percent-growth-in-participation-as-innovators-showed-up-in-las-vegas) , plus more than 4,100 exhibitors. That’s a small city’s worth of people packed into convention halls for four days.


Stadium Dance performers at the CES Consumer Electronics Show Las Vegas


But chances are that you’ve never set foot in the place. CES is[trade-only and not open to the general public](https://www.ces.tech/About-CES/Registration-Information.aspx) , so your customers won’t be there. But should you attend it? Is the networking really worth it?


That's what we are going to help you find out.


## What is CES, and what does CES stand for now?


CES is a yearly trade show where tech companies show off the products they plan to sell. It’s owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), which calls it the only trade show that covers the entire tech landscape at one event. The very first one took place in June 1967 in New York City. So yes, CES is older than the internet.


You'll find many exhibitors here. CES 2026 itself included BMW, xCaterpillar, John Deere, and more. Here's the best of CES 2026 if you are interested -


But CES isn’t just a gadget fair for tech nerds. Senior-level executives made up 52% of CES 2026 attendees, and the show now has a retail side too. CES 2026 ran a[Retail Conference Track](https://tynmagazine.com/?p=233957) with sessions on social shopping, the future of search at retail with AWS, and the AI-powered store with Target.


Though one thing you can be absolutely sure about- CES isn’t is a launch day. Plenty of products shown on stage are prototypes, and some of them never get to see the light of day.


**Fun fact:** Samsung has been showing versions of its rolling robot Ballie for[nearly five years](https://fastcompanyme.com/?p=35711) without shipping it.

## Does the show affect your sales?


Yes, and many studies call[CES one of the biggest forces pushing product prices down](https://www.consumeraffairs.com/news/why-right-now-is-a-rare-perfect-storm-for-tv-deals-011526.html) each January.


The event is like a starting gun. Once the keynotes end, a predictable cycle kicks off for anything that gets a new model at the show, and TVs are the clearest example. Most new TVs are announced at CES in January and carry a “spring” release date. For LG, pre-orders open around February to March at full MSRP, and the new models reach stores around March to April.


Here’s what the horoscopes predict for your store:


- **CES week (early January) -** The headlines roll in, and suddenly your perfectly good inventory has aged a whole year in the shopper's mind. Your TVs haven't changed overnight, but apparently, their reputation has. A little pre-show clearance planning and some extra love for your current product pages could save you from a post-show panic sale.
- **Late January to February -** Welcome to the price-cutting season. Last year's TVs start looking like yesterday's news, even when the actual upgrades are barely worth writing about. And when shoppers find the same SKU at three different stores, things can get difficult for you. Nobody wants to be the retailer still holding out at full price while everyone else is waving around discounts.
- **February to March -** Pre-orders open, and the new models get their moment in the spotlight. Full price, shiny promises, and plenty of excitement. Just make sure the product has a real ship date before you start taking orders.
- **March to April -** The new models finally hit the shelves. By now, your old inventory should ideally be enjoying its retirement somewhere other than your warehouse.
- **And if you don't sell TVs,** CES can still crash your party. If you sell soundbars, wall mounts, gaming gear, or smart home accessories? You're close enough to the TV business to catch the splash when shoppers start planning their next big-screen upgrade.


### Why “coming soon” changes what shoppers will pay today


Researchers have a badass name for products you can see but can’t buy yet: phantom products.


A[2019 study found](https://econpapers.repec.org/article/inmormnsc/v_3a65_3ay_3a2019_3ai_3a8_3ap_3a3776-3799.htm) that simply preannouncing a product can change consumer choice, because the unavailable product still sits in the shopper’s mind and shifts the reference point they use to judge everything else. More importantly for you, preannouncement does more than push people to postpone. It changes their preference for the products available right now, even among shoppers who don’t wait. A good example of this is the iPhone.


When Apple announced the iPhone on January 9, 2007,[people reportedly held on to their old phones](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/podcast/knowledge-at-wharton-podcast/new-products-like-the-iphone-announce-early-or-go-for-the-surprise-rollout/) rather than buy an alternative. One Wharton professor even mentioned a colleague who continued using his old Treo because he was waiting for the iPhone.


Photo taken at Tice's Corner Marketplace on the day of the original iPhone release. Credit: William J Sisti


A second study explains why the hype price can be misleading - when a purchase feels far away, as it does with a preannouncement,[people read a high price as a sign of quality](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/805073) .


And if you want proof, this has been happening for decades: in the early 1990s, TV sales were depressed by talk of HDTV, which didn’t become widespread for another 15 years. That’s a long time to wait for a better picture.


## If CES is such an influential event, should you go?


Our honest take is that most online sellers don’t need to go.


CES is worth the trip if you sell consumer tech or accessories and the brands you stock exhibit there. It’s a rare chance to meet suppliers face to face, and people pack their calendars. CTA’s CEO Gary Shapiro said[one exhibitor told him she had 37 meetings](https://tradeshowexecutive.com/ces-holds-largest-edition-since-covid-19-pandemic-in-2026/) in just two and a half days.


If you’re mainly after ecommerce lessons, the retail track is a small slice of a show with over 4,100 exhibitors, and you can follow the big announcements from your desk. In that case, the show you might actually want is the one right after it - the NRF.


### CES vs NRF for online sellers


NRF 2027 is retail’s Big Show, running from January 10 to 12 in New York; it is the National Retail Federation’s annual show and takes place a day after CES wraps up.


**CES 2027**


**NRF 2027**

Where

## How to register for CES 2027 (and who can attend)


In case you still decide to go, here's how to register for CES 2027. But before you book a flight to Vegas, there’s a small matter of getting in.


**Step 1: Make sure you qualify -** CES is not open to the public. It is a trade-only event for people 18 or older who are affiliated with the consumer technology industry, and you have to meet the requirements for the registration type you pick: industry attendee, media or exhibitor personnel. As for who can attend CES in practice,[event guides list](https://www.ces.tech/attendee-guides/registration-information/) retail buyers, manufacturers, marketing professionals and business executives among the usual attendees and say you may be asked for proof such as a business card or a corporate email address.


**Step 2: Pick your pass -** The price climbs the longer you wait, so procrastinators pay a “should’ve registered in November” tax.


**Pass**


**Best for**


**Early price**


**Later price**


Standard Pass


Walking the show floor and catching keynotes


$149 through Nov. 30


$349 from Dec. 1 to Jan. 9


Premium Pass


Sitting in on every conference session and track


$1,450 through Nov. 30


$1,750 from Dec. 1 to Jan. 9


**Step 3: Register only through the official site -** CES attracts scammers the way a free buffet attracts conference attendees. CTA has named Maritz as the only official[registration vendor for CES 2027](https://registration.experientevent.com/showCES271/Wizard/Landing) , and all registration emails come directly from CES. If a “registration service” emails you first, delete it.


**Step 4: Ask your suppliers for a discount code -** Exhibitors get customer invitation codes worth $149 off registration, valid through December 31, 2026. If a brand you stock is exhibiting, a quick email to your rep could save you the money.


**Step 5: Pick up your badge before you head to the show -** You’ll need a government-issued photo ID; nobody can collect a badge on your behalf, and pickup at the airport or select hotels saves you from the lines at the venues. One last thing to put in your calendar: if you forget to cancel by December 9, 2026 or don’t attend, you still pay.


## What happens in Vegas shows up in your store


Whether you fly to Las Vegas or not, CES hands your shoppers a new measuring stick. From January on, every TV and soundbar in your store gets compared with a newer model that’s still months away from shipping, and on a spec sheet, last year’s version will lose that fight every time.


You can’t win that comparison on features, and racing other stores to the lowest clearance price only eats into your margin. What you can change is what comes with the purchase. A shopper buying last year’s model at a discount is already getting a great deal, but part of them wonders whether they’re settling for something that will feel old by spring. ## Frequently Asked Questions


**1. Is CES open to the public?**
No. CES is a trade-only event for people aged 18 and older who are affiliated with the consumer technology industry.[ces](https://www.ces.tech/About-CES/Registration-Information.aspx)


**2. When is CES 2027?**
CES 2027 takes place January 6 to 9, 2027, across the Las Vegas Convention Center and other venues in Las Vegas.[ces](https://www.ces.tech/about)


**3. What does CES stand for?**
It originally stood for Consumer Electronics Show. Today, the show simply goes by CES, since it covers far more than electronics.


**4. When do CES products come out?**
It depends on the product. Most TVs announced at CES carry a spring release date, while concept products may arrive years later or not at all.
